4900: from σύν and ἐλαύνω; to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation):--+ set at one again.
4901: from σύν and ἐπιμαρτυρέω; to testify further jointly, i.e. unite in adding evidence:--also bear witness.
4902: middle voice from σύν and a primary (to follow); to attend (travel) in company with:--accompany.
4903: from συνεργός; to be a fellow-worker, i.e. co-operate:--help (work) with, work(-er) together.
4904: from a presumed compound of σύν and the base of ἔργον; a co-laborer, i.e. coadjutor:--companion in labour, (fellow-)helper(-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow.
4905: from σύν and ἔρχομαι; to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specially), cohabit (conjugally):--accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort.
4906: from σύν and ἐσθίω (including its alternate); to take food in company with:--eat with.
4907: from συνίημι; a mental putting together, i.e. intelligence or (concretely) the intellect:--knowledge, understanding.
4908: from συνίημι; mentally put (or putting) together, i.e. sagacious:--prudent. Compare φρόνιμος.
4909: from σύν and εὐδοκέω; to think well of in common, i.e. assent to, feel gratified with:--allow, assent, be pleased, have pleasure.
4910: from σύν and a derivative of a presumed compound of εὖ and a derivative of ἔχω (meaning to be in good condition, i.e. (by implication) to fare well, or feast); to entertain sumptuously in company with, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to revel together:--feast with.
4911: from σύν and ἐφίστημι; to stand up together, i.e. to resist (or assault) jointly:--rise up together.
4912: from σύν and ἔχω; to hold together, i.e. to compress (the ears, with a crowd or siege) or arrest (a prisoner); figuratively, to compel, perplex, afflict, preoccupy:--constrain, hold, keep in, press, lie sick of, stop, be in a strait, straiten, be taken with, throng.
4913: middle voice from σύν and the base of ἡδονή; to rejoice in with oneself, i.e. feel satisfaction concerning:--delight.
4914: from a compound of σύν and ἦθος; mutual habituation, i.e. usage:--custom.
4915: from σύν and a derivative of ἡλικία; a co-aged person, i.e. alike in years:--equal.
4916: from σύν and θάπτω; to inter in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate spiritually (to Christ by a sepulture as to sin):--bury with.
4917: from σύν and thlao (to crush); to dash together, i.e. shatter:--break.
4918: from σύν and θλίβω; to compress, i.e. crowd on all sides:--throng.
4919: from σύν and (to crumble); to crush together, i.e. (figuratively) to dispirit:--break.
4920: from σύν and (to send); to put together, i.e. (mentally) to comprehend; by implication, to act piously:-- consider, understand, be wise.
4921: from σύν and ἵστημι (including its collateral forms); to set together, i.e. (by implication) to introduce (favorably), or (figuratively) to exhibit; intransitively, to stand near, or (figuratively) to constitute:--approve, commend, consist, make, stand (with).
4922: from σύν and ὁδεύω; to travel in company with:--journey with.
4923: from a compound of σύν and ὁδός ("synod"); companionship on a journey, i.e. (by implication), a caravan:--company.
4924: from σύν and οἰκέω; to reside together (as a family):--dwell together.
4925: from σύν and οἰκοδομέω; to construct, i.e. (passively) to compose (in company with other Christians, figuratively):--build together.
4926: from σύν and ὁμιλέω; to converse mutually:--talk with.
4927: from σύν and a derivative of a compound of the base of 3674 and the base of ὅριον; to border together, i.e. adjoin:--join hard.
4928: from συνέχω; restraint, i.e. (figuratively) anxiety:--anguish, distress.
4929: from σύν and τάσσω; to arrange jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to direct:--appoint.
4930: from συντελέω; entire completion, i.e. consummation (of a dispensation):--end.
4931: from σύν and τελέω; to complete entirely; generally, to execute (literally or figuratively):--end, finish, fulfil, make.
4932: from σύν and the base of τομώτερος; to contract by cutting, i.e. (figuratively) do concisely (speedily):--(cut) short.
4933: from σύν and τηρέω; to keep closely together, i.e. (by implication) to conserve (from ruin); mentally, to remember (and obey):--keep, observe, preserve.
4934: middle voice from σύν and τίθημι; to place jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to consent (bargain, stipulate), concur:--agree, assent, covenant.
4935: adverb from a derivative of συντέμνω; concisely (briefly):--a few words.
4936: from σύν and τρέχω (including its alternate); to rush together (hastily assemble) or headlong (figuratively):--run (together, with).
4937: from σύν and the base of τρίβος; to crush completely, i.e. to shatter (literally or figuratively):--break (in pieces), broken to shivers (+ -hearted), bruise.
4938: from συντρίβω; concussion or utter fracture (properly, concretely), i.e. complete ruin:--destruction.
4939: from σύν and τροφός (in a passive sense); a fellow-nursling, i.e. comrade:--brought up with.
4940: from σύν and τυγχάνω; to chance together, i.e. meet with (reach):--come at.
4941: from συντυγχάνω; an accident; Syntyche, a Christian female:--Syntyche.
4942: from σύν and ὑποκρίνομαι; to act hypocritically in concert with:--dissemble with.
4943: from σύν and a derivative of a compound of ὑπό and the base of ἔργον; to be a co-auxiliary, i.e. assist:--help together.
4944: from σύν and ὠδίνω; to have (parturition) pangs in company (concert, simultaneously) with, i.e. (figuratively) to sympathize (in expectation of relief from suffering):--travail in pain together.
4945: from a compound of σύν and ὀμνύω; a swearing together, i.e. (by implication) a plot:--comspiracy.
4946: plural of uncertain derivation; Syracuse, the capital of Sicily:--Syracuse.
4947: probably of Hebrew origin (צֹר); Syria (i.e. Tsyria or Tyre), a region of Asia:--Syria.
4948: from the same as Συρία; a Syran (i.e. probably Tyrian), a native of Syria:--Syrian.
4949: feminine of a compound of Σύρος and the same as Φοινίκη; a Syro-phœnician woman, i.e. a female native of Phœnicia in Syria:--Syrophenician.
4950: from σύρω; a shoal (from the sand drawn thither by the waves), i.e. the Syrtis Major or great bay on the north coast of Africa:--quicksands.
4951: probably akin to αἱρέομαι; to trail:--drag, draw, hale.
4952: from σύν and σπαράσσω; to rend completely, i.e. (by analogy) to convulse violently:--throw down.
4953: neuter of a compound of σύν and the base of σημαίνω; a sign in common, i.e. preconcerted signal:--token.
4954: from σύν and σῶμα; of a joint body, i.e. (figuratively) a fellow-member of the Christian community:--of the same body.
4955: from a compound of σύν and a derivative of στάσις; a fellow-insurgent:--make insurrection with.
4956: from a derivative of συνιστάω; introductory, i.e. recommendatory:--of commendation.
4957: from σύν and σταυρόω; to impale in company with (literally or figuratively):--crucify with.
4958: from σύν and στέλλω; to send (draw) together, i.e. enwrap (enshroud a corpse for burial), contract (an interval):-- short, wind up.
4959: from σύν and στενάζω; to moan jointly, i.e. (figuratively) experience a common calamity:--groan together.
4960: from σύν and στοιχέω; to file together (as soldiers in ranks), i.e. (figuratively) to correspond to:--answer to.
4961: from σύν and στρατιώτης; a co-campaigner, i.e. (figuratively) an associate in Christian toil:--fellowsoldier.
4962: from σύν and στρέφω; to twist together, i.e. collect (a bundle, a crowd):--gather.
4963: from συστρέφω; a twisting together, i.e. (figuratively) a secret coalition, riotous crowd:--+ band together, concourse.
4964: from σύν and a derivative of σχῆμα; to fashion alike, i.e. conform to the same pattern (figuratively):--conform to, fashion self according to.
4965: of Hebrew origin (שֵׁכָר); Sychar (i.e. Shekar), a place in Palestine:--Sychar.
4966: of Hebrew origin (שְׁכֶם); Sychem (i.e. Shekem), the name of a Canaanite and of a place in Palestine:--Sychem.
4967: from σφάζω; butchery (of animals for food or sacrifice, or (figuratively) of men (destruction)):--slaughter.
4968: neuter of a derivative of σφαγή; a victim (in sacrifice):--slain beast.
4969: a primary verb; to butcher (especially an animal for food or in sacrifice) or (generally) to slaughter, or (specially), to maim (violently):--kill, slay, wound.
4970: neuter plural of (violent; of uncertain derivation) as adverb; vehemently, i.e. in a high degree, much:-- exceeding(-ly), greatly, sore, very.
4971: adverb from the same as σφόδρα; very much:--exceedingly.
4972: from σφραγίς; to stamp (with a signet or private mark) for security or preservation (literally or figuratively); by implication, to keep secret, to attest:--(set a, set to) seal up, stop.
4973: probably strengthened from φράσσω; a signet (as fencing in or protecting from misappropriation); by implication, the stamp impressed (as a mark of privacy, or genuineness), literally or figuratively:--seal.
4974: neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as (a ball, "sphere"; compare the feminine , a hammer); the ankle (as globular):--ancle bone.
4975: neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of ἔχω as adverb; nigh, i.e. nearly:--almost.
4976: from the alternate of ἔχω; a figure (as a mode or circumstance), i.e. (by implication) external condition:--fashion.
4977: apparently a primary verb; to split or sever (literally or figuratively):--break, divide, open, rend, make a rent.
4978: from σχίζω; a split or gap ("schism"), literally or figuratively:--division, rent, schism.
4979: diminutive of (a rush or flag-plant; of uncertain derivation); a rushlet, i.e. grass-withe or tie (generally):--small cord, rope.
4980: from σχολή; to take a holiday, i.e. be at leisure for (by implication, devote oneself wholly to); figuratively, to be vacant (of a house):--empty, give self.
4981: probably feminine of a presumed derivative of the alternate of ἔχω; properly, loitering (as a withholding of oneself from work) or leisure, i.e. (by implication) a "school" (as vacation from physical employment):--school.
4982: from a primary (contraction for obsolete , "safe"); to save, i.e. deliver or protect (literally or figuratively):--heal, preserve, save (self), do well, be (make) whole.
4983: from σώζω; the body (as a sound whole), used in a very wide application, literally or figuratively:--bodily, body, slave.
4985: adverb from σωματικός; corporeally or physically:--bodily.
4986: from the base of σώζω and πατήρ; of a safe father; Sopatrus, a Christian:--Sopater. Compare Σωσίπατρος.
4987: from another form of σορός; to pile up (literally or figuratively):--heap, load.
4988: from the base of σώζω and that of σθενόω; of safe strength; Sosthenes, a Christian:--Sosthenes.
4989: prolongation for Σώπατρος; Sosipatrus, a Christian:--Sosipater.
4990: from σώζω; a deliverer, i.e. God or Christ:--saviour.
4991: feminine of a derivative of σωτήρ as (properly, abstract) noun; rescue or safety (physically or morally):--deliver, health, salvation, save, saving.
4992: neuter of the same as σωτηρία as (properly, concretely) noun; defender or (by implication) defence:--salvation.
4993: from σώφρων; to be of sound mind, i.e. sane, (figuratively) moderate:--be in right mind, be sober (minded), soberly.
4994: from σώφρων; to make of sound mind, i.e. (figuratively) to discipline or correct:--teach to be sober.
4995: from σωφρονίζω; discipline, i.e. self-control:--sound mind.
4996: adverb from σώφρων; with sound mind, i.e. moderately:--soberly.
4997: from σώφρων; soundness of mind, i.e. (literally) sanity or (figuratively) self-control:--soberness, sobriety.
4998: from the base of σώζω and that of φρήν; safe (sound) in mind, i.e. self-controlled (moderate as to opinion or passion):--discreet, sober, temperate.
4999: plural of Latin origin; huts or wooden-walled buildings; Tabernæ:--taverns.
